ideas.title: Doc DX Grader
ideas.summary: Paste any developer docs URL and get an instant A-F Developer Experience report across five dimensions, with Claude API pinpointing specific sentences and suggesting concrete fixes.
ideas.description: A React web app where you drop in the URL (or paste the text) of any developer documentation page and receive a structured DX quality report graded A-F across five dimensions: getting-started speed, code example completeness, error scenario coverage, parameter clarity, and conceptual overview depth. Claude API reads the page content, quotes specific problem sentences, and generates 2-3 actionable improvement suggestions per dimension. A shareable report link lets you send the results to a docs team.
keyFeatures: Five-dimension scorecard (getting-started, code examples, error coverage, parameter clarity, overview depth) with letter grades
Quoted citations from the actual docs text for each issue found
2-3 concrete improvement suggestions per dimension generated by Claude API
Shareable report URL stored in Supabase so you can send results to a docs team
Side-by-side before/after preview showing a rewritten example section
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Flask backend for URL fetching and Claude API calls, Supabase for saving/sharing reports
ideas.whyInteresting: Every developer has hit documentation that wastes an hour of their time, but giving specific, structured feedback to docs teams is hard — this makes it a one-click action and produces output concrete enough to act on.
ideas.inspiredBy: HN 'Ask HN: What developer tool do you wish existed in 2026?' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46345827) and the explosion of AI-generated docs that are often incomplete or inconsistent

ideas.title: Pair Programming Pulse
ideas.summary: Submit a pair programming session transcript and receive an AI-generated collaboration quality report covering driver/navigator balance, communication patterns, and stuck-point analysis, with a class-wide heatmap for instructors.
ideas.description: A web app where student pairs paste or upload the text log from any paired coding session (VS Code Live Share chat, Zoom transcript, or a plain text log). Claude API analyzes the exchange and produces a structured collaboration quality report: estimated driver-to-navigator time ratio, frequency and quality of think-alouds, how the pair handled blockers, and specific moments where communication broke down. Instructors get a class-wide dashboard showing pair effectiveness per assignment, surfacing which student pairings need coaching.
keyFeatures: Transcript upload (plain text, JSON, or Zoom .vtt) with automatic speaker labeling
Claude API analysis measuring think-aloud rate, question quality, and blocker-handling patterns
Per-session PDF report with timestamped highlight clips and rubric scores
Instructor dashboard showing class-wide pair effectiveness heatmap per assignment
Anonymized comparison so students can see how their session compares to the class median
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind frontend, Flask backend, Claude API for transcript analysis, Supabase for session storage and instructor dashboard, PDF export via Puppeteer
ideas.whyInteresting: Pair programming is taught in nearly every CS course but almost never assessed — grading the code tells you nothing about whether the collaboration happened. This gives instructors a scalable window into the actual pairing process.
ideas.inspiredBy: HN 'Ask HN: What are you working on? (June 2026)' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48528779) discussion on developer collaboration analytics, and HackAbility AI for Accessibility 2026 pushing hands-on skills assessment

ideas.title: WebGPU Shader Studio
ideas.summary: Students build a browser-native WGSL compute shader playground with animated thread-group visualization, CPU vs. GPU benchmarks, and an AI coach explaining each pipeline stage — culminating in a shared gallery of parallel algorithm implementations.
ideas.description: A multi-week classroom project where students implement a full in-browser WGSL compute shader development environment using the WebGPU API. The app includes a Monaco editor for writing shaders, an animated canvas that visualizes thread-group execution as a live grid of colored cells, and a benchmarking panel that compares shader runtime against a JavaScript CPU baseline. A Claude API assistant explains what each pipeline stage does, flags common WGSL pitfalls, and suggests optimization strategies. Students complete a curriculum of five challenges (parallel reduction, prefix scan, matrix multiply, bitonic sort, image blur) and publish their fastest solutions to a class-wide gallery.
keyFeatures: Monaco editor with WGSL syntax highlighting and error underlining
Animated thread-group visualization showing dispatch dimensions and workgroup occupancy
CPU vs. GPU benchmark panel with real execution times and speedup ratio
Claude API assistant that explains each shader stage, flags WGSL errors, and suggests optimizations
Five graded challenge levels (parallel reduction through image blur) with automated correctness tests
Class gallery where students publish and star each other's fastest implementations
ideas.techStack: Vanilla JS or React + Vite for the UI, WebGPU API (native browser), Monaco Editor (npm), Claude API for the AI coach, Supabase for the challenge gallery and leaderboard
ideas.whyInteresting: WebGPU reached stable support in all major browsers in 2025 but almost no CS curriculum has caught up — this project teaches students a genuinely modern skill (GPU compute) while building something visually impressive that runs entirely in a browser tab.
ideas.inspiredBy: HN 'Show HN: ChartGPU – WebGPU-powered charting library' and 'Show HN: A game where you build a GPU' (https://news.ycombinator.com/front), plus the growing list of WebGPU compute tools on GitHub trending June 2026
